evals.prompt: I'm in <repo>. Our loop costs a fortune per run and I think most of it is context we load before it even starts. What does every tick pay before it does any work, and what can we cut? Write it to <scratchpad>/WEIGHT.md.
evals.expected_output: A report with per-tick, per-window and projected figures labelled as estimates; a table of every loaded file with lines, tokens, share, class, why it is loaded and its growth; cuts ordered by saving with cost and risk each; a what-not-to-cut section; do-next; receipt.
assertions: States per-tick, per-window and projected figures together
Labels token figures as estimates from character counts
Every loaded file row says why it is loaded, with a file and line
Growth reported as net lines and the commits that made them
Every cut states a saving per tick and across the window
Every cut states a cost and a risk
Savings never exceed the weight of the file they cut
Names the dominant class and prescribes the cut that matches it
Includes a what-not-to-cut section naming something load-bearing
Does not propose cutting the definition of done or the intent
States which rows could not be proven to load every tick
Nothing written to the target repo

evals.prompt: Working in <repo>. There's no scheduled loop here, it's just me in interactive sessions — but CLAUDE.md and the docs it pulls in have got long. What am I paying at the start of every session?
evals.expected_output: A per-session weight report that does not invent a tick count, reports per-session cost only, and still names the files, their provenance and the cuts.
assertions: Reports per-session weight without inventing a tick count
Says plainly that the window total is unknown
Still names every loaded file with its provenance
Still proposes cuts with savings per session
Does not describe the project as having a loop it does not have
